programme.title: Downstream
programme.sub-title: Shepherdsville, KY Bullitt County: Wine, Whiskey & Wild Part 2
programme.desc: The second part of our Bullitt County visit will begin at the longest g-cart track in the US followed by a visit to the MillaNova and Wight Meyer wineries. Carrie will paddle the Salt River with a special guest who shares some little known history about the river which powered several distilleries and yes, quite a bit of salt. This is the second of a two-part special featuring Shepherdsville and Bullitt County Kentucky.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: The Orkney Islands lie just off the North Coast of Scotland. The 70 islands are surrounded by the Atlantic and the North Sea. The landscape is made up of lush hills; steep cliffs arise in the south. Only 21,000 people live here, but there are plenty more sheep and cattle.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: In Old-Norse, its name means Isle of Cloud, or Misty Isle. Legend says that God boasted of its beauty. The Isle of Skye embodies everything that makes Scotland unique. In the past, life in this inhospitable place was difficult. Since then much has changed, not least thanks to the bridge linking it to the mainldn. The island is now home to many artists and creatives.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: To the north-west of Wales lies Anglesey, a beautiful corner of the United Kingdom. Only 400m of water separates Anglesey from the mainland, although it feels completely secluded. The 200km coastline is a designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and an important habitat for flora and fauna.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: The essence of Great Britain’s landscape and character can be found here on the Isle of Wight. Many lead a very traditional British way of life. Equestrian sports are part of this heritage. We meet a renowned horse breeder who is preparing to compete in the island's first top international competition.

programme.title: Isles of the Queen
programme.desc: Paradisiacal seas, reefs and exquisite sandy beaches: the Bermuda islands are the most northerly of all the Caribbean islands. Since the 17th century, the islands have belong to the British Crown. Then and today, they represent a vital bridgehead into America. Here, the Queen still reigns – with pomp and splendour.
